highlights.content: ![A performance comparison chart released by Krafton. (Source: Krafton)](https://cdn.thelec.net/news/photo/202611/15933_16308_5530.png) Krafton released the full version of its internally developed large language model (LLM), Raon-1 mini, on Nov. 25. According to the company, Raon-1 mini is an artificial intelligence (AI) model developed entirely in-house, from model architecture design to training. It adopts a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture that activates only 4 billion of its 30 billion parameters for computation. Combined with Krafton’s proprietary linear attention technology, the architecture improves response speed and reduces inference costs. Krafton said the full version offers improved reasoning and complex task execution capabilities compared with the preview version. It scored 64.9 on MultiChallenge, a benchmark measuring a model’s ability to follow user instructions and constraints across multiple conversational turns, up 5.9 points from the preview version. According to Krafton, the model outperformed all six comparable overseas models. The model also scored 72.3 and 55.9 on GDPval and BrowseComp Plus, respectively, which evaluate AI agents’ task execution capabilities. It achieved the highest scores among comparable MoE models in both benchmarks. Krafton also added adjustable reasoning capabilities. Users can select from six reasoning levels depending on task complexity. The model answers simple questions without a reasoning process while allocating more computational resources to complex tasks. Krafton released Raon-1 mini on AI model-sharing platform Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license. Anyone can download the model for free and use it for research and commercial service development. The company also provides an environment for testing the model and an application programming interface (API). Since launching its AI model brand Raon in April, Krafton has released open-source AI models for speech and vision applications. The company plans to introduce Raon-1, a larger model than Raon-1 mini, and a real-time bidirectional speech model capable of listening and responding to users simultaneously. ![kimsungjin의 프로필 이미지](https://cdn.thelec.net/image/newsroom/default-user.png) [View other news](https://www.thelec.net/news/articleList.html?sc_area=I&sc_word=harang&view_type=sm)

highlights.content: NVIDIA researchers gave four frontier models control over their own context window, and one of them nearly tripled its score. At a 32K-token budget on OfficeQA Pro v2, GPT-6.1 Sol rose from 21% to 56% when it decided for itself when to compact its history, according to the paper ["Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34147?ref=explainx) (arXiv 2611.34147, November 25, 2026). The result is real but narrow. It holds for one model, one benchmark and a tight budget, and it fades as the window grows. This post covers what the paper did, what each model did differently, what the numbers do and do not show, and what a team building agents can test this week. ## TL;DR: what NVIDIA found | Question | Answer from the paper | |---|---| | What was tested? | Model-driven vs harness-driven context compaction in NVIDIA's open-source NOOA harness | | Which models? | GPT-6.1 Sol, Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Claude Opus 5.5 | | Headline result | GPT-6.1 Sol: 21% to 56% on OfficeQA Pro v2 at a 32K budget | | Token savings | Kimi K3: up to 41% fewer input tokens; 36M vs 62M cumulative at 32K | | Who ignored the tool? | Opus 5.5 edited its context in only 4% of tasks | | Inference finding | Suffix KV-cache reuse cut prefill compute 4 to 15% per request, with no measured accuracy change | | Biggest caveat | Small benchmarks: 90 questions and 22 competitions | ## What does "model-managed context" mean? ![A broad fan of paper strips folding into a compact accordion, picturing how model-managed context compacts agent history](https://explainx.ai/images/blog-library/context-compression.webp)A broad fan of paper strips folding into a compact accordion, picturing how model-managed context compacts agent history Most agent harnesses manage context on the model's behalf. When the window fills up, the harness triggers a compaction step. The model only writes the summary. Everything else is decided by code. The NVIDIA team studied the alternative. The model gets a context API and decides when to compact and what to compress. The paper describes the setup in the NOOA harness, short for NVIDIA Labs Object-Oriented Agents, an open-source research preview where an agent is a single Python class. NVIDIA's own [developer blog on harness design](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/six-agent-harness-capabilities-for-higher-model-performance/?ref=explainx) lists "model-callable harness APIs" as one of six capabilities of the harness, and this paper tests that idea at scale. The two strategies differ in concrete ways. - **Harness-driven baseline.** At 80% of the context budget, the harness summarizes earlier history. It keeps the initial instructions and the 10 most recent events. - **Model-driven.** The model sees a live context-usage indicator, an instruction to consider compacting at 85% usage, and a context-pressure warning as the limit nears. Its main tool is a `collapse` call that replaces a range of events with a summary. - **Archive, not delete.** Collapsed events are archived. The model can retrieve any of them later by its original tag. - **Hard budgets.** Each budget, from 8K to 512K tokens, is a hard request-size limit. If a request exceeds it, a fallback drops the oldest events and retries. After three failures the run counts as wrong. If you want the background on why this matters, our post on [Apple's SelfCompact](https://explainx.ai/blog/apple-selfcompact-self-compacting-language-model-agents-context-2026) covered the same question from a different angle: should the agent decide when to compress itself. In an essay published by the DeepMind Institute on November 19, Google DeepMind research scientist Tim Genewein sets out four ways AI might reach that level and calls for better ways to measure progress along each route.** Genewein defines artificial general intelligence (AGI) as AI that can match humans across nearly all cognitive tasks. His bar for artificial general superintelligence (ASI) is higher. A system would have to consistently outperform groups of experts on work that could take them years, using less time and fewer resources. It would have to do so across a broad range of fields. The essay draws on a technical paper, *From AGI to ASI*, which Genewein co-authored. It reflects his analysis, and the DeepMind Institute describes its essays as the views of their authors. #### **What happens when the same AI gets cheaper to run** A model’s capabilities can stay the same while the cost of using it falls. Faster hardware and more efficient software can let organizations run more copies of a system at once. Genewein calls the potential result “cognitive industrialization,” in which certain kinds of knowledge work become cheap enough to standardize and automate across sectors. In one scenario he sketches, the amount of computing power available and improvements in software efficiency could make it possible to run more than a thousand times as many agents at today’s capability level by 2030. That scenario depends on how far computing infrastructure can expand and how much more efficient the software becomes. Genewein argues that this change in the volume and speed of AI work could affect the economy on its own. For researchers tracking the effect on knowledge work, the cost of getting a task done may matter alongside what the most capable model can do. #### **More agents bring more work to coordinate** One route to superintelligence would be to organize AI agents into teams that divide the work. He argues that large groups of agents would need safeguards against manipulation, collusion and the spread of false information. #### **Bigger models face constraints in data and power** Making models larger and training them on more data is another route. (Source: Krafton)](https://cdn.thelec.net/news/photo/202611/15933_16308_5530.png) Krafton released the full version of its internally developed large language model (LLM), Raon-1 mini, on Nov. 25. According to the company, Raon-1 mini is an artificial intelligence (AI) model developed entirely in-house, from model architecture design to training. It adopts a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture that activates only 4 billion of its 30 billion parameters for computation. Combined with Krafton’s proprietary linear attention technology, the architecture improves response speed and reduces inference costs. Krafton said the full version offers improved reasoning and complex task execution capabilities compared with the preview version. It scored 64.9 on MultiChallenge, a benchmark measuring a model’s ability to follow user instructions and constraints across multiple conversational turns, up 5.9 points from the preview version. According to Krafton, the model outperformed all six comparable overseas models. The model also scored 72.3 and 55.9 on GDPval and BrowseComp Plus, respectively, which evaluate AI agents’ task execution capabilities. It achieved the highest scores among comparable MoE models in both benchmarks. Krafton also added adjustable reasoning capabilities. Users can select from six reasoning levels depending on task complexity. The model answers simple questions without a reasoning process while allocating more computational resources to complex tasks. Krafton released Raon-1 mini on AI model-sharing platform Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license. Anyone can download the model for free and use it for research and commercial service development. The company also provides an environment for testing the model and an application programming interface (API). Since launching its AI model brand Raon in April, Krafton has released open-source AI models for speech and vision applications. The company plans to introduce Raon-1, a larger model than Raon-1 mini, and a real-time bidirectional speech model capable of listening and responding to users simultaneously. ![kimsungjin의 프로필 이미지](https://cdn.thelec.net/image/newsroom/default-user.png) [View other news](https://www.thelec.net/news/articleList.html?sc_area=I&sc_word=harang&view_type=sm)

LLMs.content: Shanghai AI Laboratory has put a new open medical model on Hugging Face. **Sage-Med-Preview** is a mixture-of-experts vision-language model with **35B total and 3B active parameters**. It reads medical images, answers clinical questions, drafts radiology reports and marks findings in the image. The lab's own report says it averages **58.26 across 31 public medical multimodal benchmarks**, ahead of GPT-5.4 (52.78) and Claude Opus 4.6 (49.18). It trails GPT-6.2 Sol on several knowledge and grounding tests. Treat the numbers as the authors' claims. They come from the lab's [model card](https://huggingface.co/internlm/Sage-Med-Preview?ref=explainx) and its [101-page paper on arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34575?ref=explainx), submitted on November 25, 2026. Independent replication does not exist yet, because the model page itself was created this morning. ## TL;DR: Sage-Med-Preview at a glance | Question | Answer | |---|---| | Who made it? | The Sage-Med team at Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, led by Ming Hu per the arXiv listing | | What is it? | Medical multimodal model, 35B total and 3B active parameters, built on Intern-S2-Preview | | What does it do? | Medical question answering, image understanding, report generation, visual grounding | | Headline claim | 58.26 average over 31 public benchmarks (GPT-5.4: 52.78, Claude Opus 4.6: 49.18) | | Where does it lose? | Knowledge tests such as MMMU Pro-Med and SuperGPQA-Med, and the MedSG-Bench grounding test | | How big is the download? | About 131 GiB on first launch | | What hardware was tested? | One NVIDIA H200, BF16, 32,768-token context, vLLM | | License | Not stated on the model card or GitHub page when checked | | Clinical use? | No. The card says clinical use needs professional review and validation | ## What is Sage-Med-Preview, and why 3B active parameters matter The model sits in a family that explainx.ai has followed through the autumn. Shanghai AI Lab's science line includes [Sage-A1.5, an open 35B MoE with subagents and a verification mode](https://explainx.ai/blog/shanghai-ai-lab-sage-a1-5-35b-moe-open-weights-subagents-verification-mode-benchmarks-2026) and [Sage S2.1 Flash, a multimodal science agent](https://explainx.ai/blog/sage-s2-1-flash-shanghai-ai-lab-science-agent-november-2026). Sage-Med-Preview takes the Intern-S2-Preview base and specializes it for medicine. A mixture-of-experts model keeps many parameters on disk but runs only a few per token. Here 35B parameters are stored and about 3B are active for each token. That is why the lab stresses efficiency: the weights still need roughly 131 GiB, but the compute per answer is closer to a small dense model. The dictionary entry for [mixture of experts](https://explainx.ai/dictionary/mixture-of-experts) explains the routing idea if the term is new. The card's pitch is one model for four jobs that usually need separate systems: 1. **Medical knowledge and question answering** (text-only and image-based). 2. **Image understanding** across more than 40 modalities, from X-ray and CT to fundus photos, pathology and surgical video. 3. **Report generation**, such as a chest X-ray findings paragraph. 4. **Visual grounding**, which means drawing the region of an image that supports an answer. ## How was Sage-Med-Preview trained? LLMs.titleZh: Model-Managed Context: GPT-6.1 Sol 21% to 56% (NVIDIA) | explainx.ai Blog
LLMs.content: NVIDIA researchers gave four frontier models control over their own context window, and one of them nearly tripled its score. At a 32K-token budget on OfficeQA Pro v2, GPT-6.1 Sol rose from 21% to 56% when it decided for itself when to compact its history, according to the paper ["Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34147?ref=explainx) (arXiv 2611.34147, November 25, 2026). The result is real but narrow. It holds for one model, one benchmark and a tight budget, and it fades as the window grows. This post covers what the paper did, what each model did differently, what the numbers do and do not show, and what a team building agents can test this week. ## TL;DR: what NVIDIA found | Question | Answer from the paper | |---|---| | What was tested? | Model-driven vs harness-driven context compaction in NVIDIA's open-source NOOA harness | | Which models? | GPT-6.1 Sol, Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Claude Opus 5.5 | | Headline result | GPT-6.1 Sol: 21% to 56% on OfficeQA Pro v2 at a 32K budget | | Token savings | Kimi K3: up to 41% fewer input tokens; 36M vs 62M cumulative at 32K | | Who ignored the tool? | Opus 5.5 edited its context in only 4% of tasks | | Inference finding | Suffix KV-cache reuse cut prefill compute 4 to 15% per request, with no measured accuracy change | | Biggest caveat | Small benchmarks: 90 questions and 22 competitions | ## What does "model-managed context" mean? ![A broad fan of paper strips folding into a compact accordion, picturing how model-managed context compacts agent history](https://explainx.ai/images/blog-library/context-compression.webp)A broad fan of paper strips folding into a compact accordion, picturing how model-managed context compacts agent history Most agent harnesses manage context on the model's behalf. When the window fills up, the harness triggers a compaction step. The model only writes the summary. Everything else is decided by code. The NVIDIA team studied the alternative. The model gets a context API and decides when to compact and what to compress. The paper describes the setup in the NOOA harness, short for NVIDIA Labs Object-Oriented Agents, an open-source research preview where an agent is a single Python class. NVIDIA's own [developer blog on harness design](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/six-agent-harness-capabilities-for-higher-model-performance/?ref=explainx) lists "model-callable harness APIs" as one of six capabilities of the harness, and this paper tests that idea at scale. The two strategies differ in concrete ways. - **Harness-driven baseline.** At 80% of the context budget, the harness summarizes earlier history. It keeps the initial instructions and the 10 most recent events. - **Model-driven.** The model sees a live context-usage indicator, an instruction to consider compacting at 85% usage, and a context-pressure warning as the limit nears. Its main tool is a `collapse` call that replaces a range of events with a summary. - **Archive, not delete.** Collapsed events are archived. The model can retrieve any of them later by its original tag. - **Hard budgets.** Each budget, from 8K to 512K tokens, is a hard request-size limit. If a request exceeds it, a fallback drops the oldest events and retries. After three failures the run counts as wrong. If you want the background on why this matters, our post on [Apple's SelfCompact](https://explainx.ai/blog/apple-selfcompact-self-compacting-language-model-agents-context-2026) covered the same question from a different angle: should the agent decide when to compress itself. NVIDIA's earlier study, covered in [NVIDIA Says You Don't Need Long Context](https://explainx.ai/blog/nvidia-you-dont-need-long-context-compaction-sssm-arxiv-november-2026), argued that frequent compaction can match full-history accuracy at lower cost. ## The benchmarks: OfficeQA Pro v2 and MLE-bench Lite The paper uses two task families. **OfficeQA Pro v2** has 90 questions about U.S. federal receipts and exp...

[The second](https://en.bonikbarta.com/opinion/8EFJ6wplIcxb5bnI) proposed fixes for four specific risks. This one deals with what remains: the gaps in policy, justice for people whose data leaks and the shape of a model the country can trust and afford. The government is now treating the subject seriously. Opening the Bangladesh AI Business Summit 2026 on November 5, President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said Bangladesh must apply and innovate with AI instead of merely using it, and that work on national AI capabilities in Bangla is under way. He said a human-centric national AI policy, covering ethics, human rights and risk-based regulation, is being drafted. The prime minister’s ICT adviser has promised sovereign AI infrastructure within 12 months, open to startups, universities and students, and official plans point to computing nodes at the National Data Centre in Kaliakair, backed by eight regional centres. A president who speaks on it, a deadline and a site are what a serious programme looks like. They are also reasons to settle the safeguards before the first server is switched on. Start with the law. The Personal Data Protection Act 2026 requires consent before processing (Section 5), gives sensitive data extra protection (Section 7), limits reuse of data (Section 16) and requires breaches to be reported to the authority (Section 20). That is a real foundation. Three gaps remain. The first is the breach clock. Section 20 asks for notice within a prescribed time, and the rules that would prescribe it have not been issued. Critics say there is still no firm deadline and no regulator able to enforce one. The European Union requires notice to the regulator within 72 hours, and to affected people without undue delay when the risk to them is high (Articles 33-34). Bangladesh should adopt both this year. The second is that the Act speaks of data and says little of models. Any publicly funded language model should publish its training sources and filtering, exclude NID, health and telecom records unless anonymised and cleared, and pass an independent memorisation test before release. The third is the enforcer. The state is the largest holder of citizens’ data, and an authority that answers to the executive cannot police it. It needs a statutory footing, its own budget, an annual report to Parliament and staff who can audit a model as well as a database. Then comes the harder question: what happens when data leaks anyway? The authority can fine violators up to BDT 25 lakh, or BDT 50 lakh for a significant controller, order compensation and fine the directors and officers responsible. Appeals go to the ICT Act tribunal within 30 days. That skeleton was built for individual complaints. In 2023, the Birth and Death Registration website exposed an estimated 50 million records, and a ceiling of BDT 50 lakh means little at that scale. Five changes would help. People should be told in plain Bangla what was exposed and what to do. Victims of fraud rarely trace a scam to a single leak, so for confirmed exposure of sensitive data the law should set a minimum payment and put the burden of disproving harm on the organisation that lost the data. The EU already gives anyone who suffers damage from a breach a right to compensation (Article 82). Rights groups should be able to sue on behalf of thousands, as EU law allows (Article 80), because ordinary families cannot each afford a tribunal case. Fines, toge...

Does your app need advanced reasoning or a model that can handle routine requests? For example, you don’t need a complex reasoning model for tasks like sorting customer support tickets. But if you need to compare conflicting clauses across 50 contracts, a compact model may struggle. Does a smaller model actually give you enough performance for routine tasks? Recent research suggests that, in some cases, it can. A 2025 [EMNLP study](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.9/) compared specialized models trained through fine-tuning or instruction-tuning with general-purpose models used through prompting or in-context learning. Across eight text classification tasks, the specialized models often matched or surpassed the general-purpose baselines with around 100 labeled examples on average. However, the requirements varied significantly across tasks and increased when researchers accounted for performance variation. The study also found that larger models did not consistently perform better, which suggests model size alone is not a reliable guide. **Is Your Workflow Ready for 2027? LLMs.title: Exploring the Use of Large Language Models in Critical Discourse Analysis: A Consensus-Based Pilot Study - ACL Anthology
LLMs.titleZh: Exploring the Use of Large Language Models in Critical Discourse Analysis: A Consensus-Based Pilot Study - ACL Anthology
LLMs.content: ##### Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in the social sciences and humanities (SSH) to support the analysis of complex textual data, raising methodological questions about evaluation and interpretive reliability. This paper explores the use of LLMs in Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA), considered here as a paradigmatic case of interpretive research in SSH, through a preliminary consensus-based evaluation framework. The study reports on a pilot experiment conducted on a small, theory-driven corpus of opinion articles addressing the October 7, 2023 attack and its aftermath. An LLM is asked to answer analytically motivated questions targeting different levels of discourse structure. Its responses are compared with annotations produced by multiple human analysts and aggregated through a consensus-based procedure. The results reveal an asymmetry in model performance: while LLMs align well with human consensus on macro- and superstructural features, they struggle with microstructural phenomena involving implicit meaning. These findings support the view of LLMs as epistemic support tools rather than replacements for human interpretation. LLMs.title: Safety, accuracy, empathy, and readability of four large language models answering esophageal cancer radiotherapy adverse-effect questions: a comparative study | Scientific Reports
LLMs.titleZh: Safety, accuracy, empathy, and readability of four large language models answering esophageal cancer radiotherapy adverse-effect questions: a comparative study | Scientific Reports
LLMs.content: ## Abstract Patients receiving radiotherapy for esophageal cancer may consult large language model chatbots about treatment-related adverse effects, but the safety of their advice is uncertain. We submitted 42 researcher-developed, patient-oriented questions once each to ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Doubao through public web interfaces, obtaining 168 responses. Five blinded expert raters assessed potential harm, accuracy, and perceived empathic communication; information quality, visible source transparency, and formula-based readability were also evaluated. Twenty-one responses (12.5%) were classified as potentially unsafe; six could delay clinical assessment and ten involved potentially harmful self-management advice. Unsafe-response proportions ranged from 7.1% to 16.7% across models, with no statistically significant overall difference (Cochran’s Q = 1.981, *P* = 0.576). Median accuracy and expert-rated perceived empathic communication scores were 4 and 3 (on five-point scales) for every model. Between-model differences were statistically significant but small (accuracy: *P* = 0.001, Kendall’s W = 0.126; perceived empathic communication: *P* < 0.001, W = 0.149). Visible source-transparency indicators were limited, and formula-estimated readability differed across models. These single-query findings indicate that favorable accuracy ratings do not preclude potentially unsafe advice and cannot establish stable model rankings, patient comprehension, or clinical outcomes. ## Funding This project is supported by the following funds: National Famous Old Chinese Medicine Experts Inheritance Studio Construction Project (State TCM Human Education Letter \[2022] No. 75) \[CZ0274-02]; National Famous Chinese Medicine Inheritance Studio Construction Project (State TCM Office Human Education Letter \[2022] No. 245) \[CZ0250-01]; National “100,000 Talents” Support Program for Traditional Chinese Medicine—Qihuang Scholars (Document No. 284 \[2018] of the Ministry of Education); Henan Province High-Level Specialty Development Project in Traditional Chinese Medicine (Oncology) (cz0317-10). ## Ethics declarations ### Competing interests The authors declare no competing interests. ### Ethical standards The study assessed chatbot-generated responses to researcher-developed questions and did not involve patients or patient-level data. In accordance with applicable Chinese research ethics regulations36, the Ethics Committee of the First Affiliated Hospital of Henan University of Chinese Medicine waived the requirement for ethical review. The five expert evaluators were informed of the study procedures and provided written informed consent. The study was conducted in accordance with applicable institutional and national ethical guidelines and the relevant principles of the Declaration of Helsinki. ## Additional information ### Publisher’s note Springer Nature remains neutral with regard to jurisdictional claims in published maps and institutional affiliations. ## Supplementary Information Below is the link to the electronic supplementary material. ## Rights and permissions **Open Access** This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License, which permits use, sharing, adaptation, distribution and reproduction in any medium or format, as long as you give appropriate credit to the original author(s) and the source, provide a link to the Creative Commons licence, and indicate if changes were made. With more individual users turning to Conversational AI such as ChatGPT and Claude for simple design tasks, the companies are betting on business customers that need more sophisticated, high-quality results. Adobe, Figma and Canva are all strengthening their enterprise product lines for the AI era, according to the AI and software industry on the 27th. At Adobe Max, its biggest annual event, held in Miami, Florida, in the middle of this month, Adobe spent considerable time demonstrating how businesses use its flagship editing tools equipped with AI agents to produce content. It also shared news of collaborations with major companies including Google, Disney and Microsoft (MS). At the event, Adobe said it would introduce Adobe Creative Agent, an AI assistant that can independently handle multistep tasks in response to natural-language instructions, across its flagship editing tools, including Photoshop, Premiere and Illustrator. The company plans to use its AI-enhanced editing tools to focus on automating the production of corporate advertising and marketing content. Its goal is to create a seamless workflow in which AI agents handle repetitive, tedious production tasks while people focus on creative work. As part of that effort, Adobe added a range of AI agent-powered workflow automation features to its marketing platform, GenStudio. AI agents support project management and task allocation, and help draft campaign plans by analyzing marketing performance data and existing materials. Adobe also reached an agreement with Disney to develop a dedicated AI model. Built using Adobe's Firefly Foundry custom AI model service, the specialized model is trained on Disney's vast portfolio of character intellectual property (IP). Disney decided to use the model in developing theme parks and cruises. AI Product.content: # Adobe Integrates PDF Editing and AI Summaries: How Acrobat Is Transforming Enterprise Document Work ![Adobe Integrates PDF Editing and AI Summaries: How Acrobat Is Transforming Enterprise Document Work](https://img.biggo.com/hSpzkgJDGv4DtNS6AevTN2PYHSxTX6vnLkmM6bslouY/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTExLzcyOWMwYzVhLWY1YjktNDQ0My05M2E1LTkzYjA5MzNiMmRiZF8xNzk1NzQyOTI3X2RlZmF1bHQud2VicA.webp) Adobe's Acrobat is evolving from a mere PDF viewing tool into an enterprise document productivity platform. In addition to PDF editing, its integration of generative AI-powered summarization and cross-document question answering is winning praise from enterprise teams that routinely handle contracts and financial reports. The catalyst was Expert Consumers, which publishes product reviews for consumers, selecting Acrobat as an AI document assistant for enterprise teams. The evaluation covered PDF editing, AI summarization, and document productivity features. Among Acrobat's core features, "Edit PDF" deserves particular attention. For older materials whose original Word or PowerPoint files can no longer be found, or for PDFs created by other departments or outside parties, users can directly modify body text and adjust fonts and layout. The tool also handles replacing, moving, resizing, and deleting images and graphics. Its practical advantage is that minor fixes—such as updating only dates, figures, or contact information to the latest values—can be completed without hunting down the source file and re-exporting it. However, the scope of what can be edited depends on the state of the PDF. The operations available may vary depending on the fonts used, whether password protection is enabled, and the document's layout. It is best positioned not as a substitute for the source file that lets you overhaul a document, but as a feature for tidying up the necessary portions directly on the PDF. The centerpiece of the AI features is the "Acrobat AI Assistant." It lets users ask questions about PDF content in natural language, making it suited to locating specific clauses in contracts or figures and explanations in reports. Answers come with numbered citations, and selecting one highlights the relevant passage within the document, so users can verify the original wording and context on the spot. "Generative Summary" generates an overview of long PDFs and organizes key points section by section. The intended workflow is to grasp a report's main conclusions before reading the full text, then follow the references to narrow down which sections warrant close reading. Typical uses include identifying contract terms, exploring financial information, reviewing proposals and internal policies, and pre-reading project reports. The AI Assistant also supports comparing two documents and analyzing charts and tables within PDFs, and can handle documents in English, Japanese, French, German, Italian, Spanish, and Portuguese. "PDF Spaces" is what bundles information across multiple files. It consolidates multiple PDFs, links, and text into a single workspace, allowing users to ask questions of the entire set of materials. Envisioned uses include a procurement team comparing proposals from multiple vendors across documents, or an HR team referencing a policy collection and training materials in the same place. What sets it apart from conventional AI summarization is that it goes beyond summarizing a single file. On the editing side, in addition to modifying text and images, Acrobat offers spell check, find and replace, and automatic layout adjustment. It also supports reordering, inserting, and deleting pages, and mobile editing via Acrobat Reader is possible. For large-scale revisions, converting PDF to Word is effective, preserving fonts, tables, bulleted lists, and formatting. AI Product.titleZh: Ubisoft reportedly makes game teams justify leaving generative AI out - Startup Fortune
AI Product.content: *Calling a tool optional means less when turning it down takes a detailed defence. Before you roll out AI at work, look at who's being made to explain themselves.* Pitching a new game at Ubisoft now reportedly means dealing with generative AI whether you want to use it or not. Teams are expected to show how it would speed up production, or explain at length why it won't, Vertical Slice's Chris Kerr reported on Wednesday, November 25, citing several current employees who spoke anonymously for fear of reprisal. Pitches that do neither don't get approved, according to the report. Ubisoft says it isn't forcing developers to use generative AI. "We encourage our teams to explore where AI can be useful and bring value to their work. This doesn't mean that projects are required to use generative AI," the company said in a response Vertical Slice added to its story the following day. Ubisoft also said teams need to work out whether, and how, these technologies make sense for the game they want to make and the experience they want to give players. Notice that the statement never mentions pitches. It can be accurate while the report is too, because a team may be free to leave AI out and still have to earn permission to do it. Vertical Slice says the expectation came out in a presentation from company leadership to employees. In the publication's words, staff who don't want the technology must "comprehensively detail why generative AI is not suitable." A source told it Ubisoft is "not outright mandating the use of generative AI" but is all-in on it. The same source was blunter about the mood. The change in attitude among leaders, that person said, means "we all feel cornered by generative AI all the time." ![Lightricks splits itself in two as AI costs force a reset](https://startupfortune.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/sf-13093-1780661633720.jpg) [Lightricks splits itself in two as AI costs force a reset](https://startupfortune.com/lightricks-splits-itself-in-two-as-ai-costs-force-a-reset/) Lightricks is splitting its Facetune consumer app business from its LTX AI video division while cutting 75 jobs. "It's not forced, but it feels like we are heavily encouraged to use it," one developer told the outlet. Its reporting also draws on internal data putting Ubisoft's spending on generative AI tokens, the units that AI usage is typically billed in, at about $1.2 million a month and rising. Ubisoft's response doesn't confirm that figure. Money is the obvious place to look, though Ubisoft hasn't publicly tied its pitch process to costs. Its half-year results on November 19 showed net bookings of €644.7 million, down 16.5% from a year earlier. One startup is looking to fill that gap by linking planning documents to code. It’s called Manyfast. Jae-hyeok Heo, CEO of Manyfast/source=IT DongA Manyfast goes beyond document creation. IT DongA spoke with Manyfast CEO Jae-hyeok Heo about everything from how the startup got its start to its strategy for entering North America. Jae-hyeok Heo founded the design agency LeoLap in 2021 and completed more than 350 early-stage product design and planning projects over five years. Startup and corporate clients brought in plans in all sorts of formats, including Notion, Figma, hand-drawn sketches, Word, Excel and PowerPoint. That meant teams were constantly spending time clearing up misunderstandings and redoing work. The planning process already followed a clear path from requirements to wireframes and storyboards, but planners had no dedicated tool of their own, the way developers had integrated development environments (IDEs) and designers had Figma. To solve the problem, Heo began building an internal tool for product managers at LeoLap. Development began in late 2023, and the team used and tested the tool internally for more than a year before officially launching it in March 2026 as a global business-to-business software-as-a-service (SaaS) offering. Infra & Chips.content: # Asia made a big AI bet on Nvidia. What happens now? Jensen Huang's extraordinary return as Nvidia's boss rocked not only its shares in New York but also sent shockwaves through the artificial intelligence (AI) industry around the world. Those jolts were felt particularly in Asia as the saga highlighted the region's huge exposure to the technology. Tech-heavy stock indexes in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan went on a rollercoaster ride this week. Markets soared after a [near-trillion dollar surge](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cq62pn6j42jko) in Nvidia's share price but then slumped as concerns about political and regulatory scrutiny hit investor confidence. The chipmaker is a "symbolic bellwether" of the AI trade that is fast becoming key to places like South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore and Malaysia," says Dylan Loh, an international studies lecturer at Nanyang Technological University. From chip manufacturing to data centres to foreign investments, AI has become a strategic priority for these economies - and they are now increasingly dependent on Nvidia's fortunes. ## Nvidia is everywhere In Nvidia, the AI industry has the unrivalled power of cutting-edge chips and the financial clout that turned it into "the bank of AI". And in Huang, it has a high-profile evangelist. That combination has put it at the heart of the AI ecosystem in more ways than one. For one, Nvidia was able to grow rapidly by outsourcing chip production instead of having to spend heavily to build its own manufacturing plants. It contracts out most of its production to Taiwanese chipmaking giant TSMC. That means Taiwan is vulnerable to changes in AI tech demand, says Paul Cavey, founder of Taipei-based research firm East Asia Econ. "The surge in \[Taiwan's] real economic growth since 2024 has been because of the big increase in AI related exports". Huang said earlier this year that Nvidia plans to invest around $150bn (£114.4bn) a year in Taiwan at a launch to celebrate the firm's planned headquarters on the island. To a lesser extent, South Korea and Japan are also exposed to the industry, Cavey adds. They are among its suppliers of key components such as memory chips and testing equipment, with firms like Samsung and SK Hynix making the firm's processors. On top of that, Nvidia is a financial backstop and major lender to companies in the AI supply chain. ![Getty Images The DayOne Data Centers Ltd. campus in the Kempas Tech Park, Johor, Malaysia, on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/fc11/live/ba2cd510-e9ec-11f1-b6b1-7951f81135eb.jpg.webp)Getty Images It is difficult to overstate the role Nvidia, with Huang at its helm, has played in the region's AI industry. Nvidia's chips fill its data centres, power its AI models and feed the companies making cars and electronics. "Asia isn't just a customer base for Nvidia. It is an indispensable engine of the company's AI dominance because of East Asia's semiconductor manufacturing and memory ecosystems," Loh says. In the Asia-Pacific region, the data centre market, which is largely powered by Nvidia chips, is in the midst of an "unprecedented boom", according to [market research group CBRE](https://www.cbre.com.sg/insights/reports/2026-asia-pacific-data-centre-trends-and-outlook?gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=22740080622&gbraid=0AAAAABJKBd4o1u9qgGTURQlobueIy0JvC&gclid=CjwKCAiAq5rYBhB-EiwAhj1RdsP-Hvp1a8i0bN8fYYwmhJMJHQippbNYdi8TH5VKrMrNkxTr_psADhoCmYEQAvD_BwE). The volume of investment has been rising steadily in recent years to reach a record of $11.6bn (£8.85bn) in 2025. In South East Asia, Singapore-based AI company Megaspeed had become the region's biggest buyer of Nvidia chips before it was accused of smuggling them to China. Megaspeed has said it "conducts legitimate and lawful business" and has "retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation". Infra & Chips.titleZh: NVIDIA's Data Center Sales Jump 110%: Can NVDA Keep the Pace Ahead?
Infra & Chips.content: # NVIDIA's Data Center Sales Jump 110%: Can NVDA Keep the Pace Ahead? **NVIDIA Corporation**'s NVDA Data Center business remains its biggest growth engine. In the recently reported results for third-quarter fiscal 2027, the Data Center end market's revenues climbed 110% year over year to a record $107.6 billion. The segment also grew 21% sequentially, accounting for 93% of the company's $115.8 billion total revenues. Increased spending by cloud providers, AI developers and enterprises seeking more computing power mainly drove Data Center's revenues higher. Both major customer groups contributed. Hyperscale revenues rose 71% year over year to $60.1 billion, while AI Clouds, Industrial and Enterprise revenues surged 195% to $47.5 billion. NVIDIA stated that demand was supported by Blackwell Ultra systems, the early rollout of its Vera Rubin platform and standalone Vera CPUs (central processing units). Rubin generated nearly $20 billion in its first quarter of production shipments, marking the fastest product ramp-up in company history. The outlook remains strong. NVIDIA expects fourth-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, and management forecasted that fiscal 2028 revenues could grow about 75% year over year. This outlook suggests customers are continuing to invest heavily in AI computing capacity. Still, sustaining this pace will require careful execution. NVIDIA's supply commitments climbed to $390 billion, mainly due to multi-year memory procurement. Data center construction, power availability and customer financing may influence deployment schedules. Overall, demand supports further growth, but supply execution and infrastructure readiness will determine how much of that opportunity NVIDIA can capture. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for NVDA's fiscal 2027 and 2028 revenues indicates year-over-year growth of 95.4% and 72.1%, respectively. ## AMD and AVGO: Rivals Challenging NVDA in AI Data Centers **Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.** AMD and **Broadcom Inc.** AVGO are two of NVIDIA's major competitors in the AI data center space. Advanced Micro Devices is emerging as a strong challenger in AI computing with its Instinct GPUs (graphics processing units) and EPYC server processors. In the third quarter of 2026, AMD's total revenues soared 44.7% year over year to $13.38 billion. Advanced Micro Devices' Data Center revenues surged 97% year over year to a record $8.55 billion, contributing approximately 64% of total revenues. Data Center revenues were driven by expanding deployments of EPYC processors across cloud and enterprise workloads and initial shipments of Instinct MI450 Series graphics processing units (GPUs). AMD is also expanding its Helios rack-scale systems to compete in large AI infrastructure deployments.
